prerequisites: Basic knowledge of electromagnetism provided by an introductory physics course
Basic knowledge of DC and AC circuit theory

learning_outcomes.text: Provide basic technical knowledge and skills in electromagnetic propagation, both guided and in free space, as well as in antennas.
Develop the ability to analyze and design, also using electromagnetic simulators and basic instrumentation, transmission lines, metallic waveguides, optical fibers, basic antennas, and radio links.
Understand physical phenomena, basic mathematical models, and key descriptive parameters of propagation (lines, waveguides, free-space) and radiation (antennas).
Comprehend and use information from textbooks or technical reports on transmission lines, waveguides, free-space propagation, and antennas.
Understand technical descriptions of simple systems involving transmission lines, waveguides, free-space propagation, and antennas.
Identify and apply appropriate mathematical models, basic methodologies, and descriptive parameters for analyzing, describing, or designing electromagnetic systems.
Use an electromagnetic simulator to analyze and design simple systems involving transmission lines and antennas.
Critically evaluate the concepts and analysis tools presented during the course.
Assess the results of mathematical models and analysis methods, considering the approximations made.
Analyze and critically evaluate results from electromagnetic simulators and network analyzer measurements, considering non-idealities.
Present knowledge clearly and logically, using appropriate technical language.
Effectively communicate results from simulations or laboratory measurements.

syllabus_topics: The concept of wave and propagation
The wave as a disturbance capable of propagating and performing work at a distance
Damped and undamped sinusoidal waves, standing waves
Descriptive parameters in the time domain
Descriptive parameters in the frequency domain
Maxwell’s equations in static and time-varying fields
Propagation in good dielectrics and good conductors
Poynting vector in time and frequency domains
The antenna as a transformer between guided and free waves
Near and far field of an antenna
Aperture antennas, horn antennas, and parabolic antennas
Radio link design and Friis formula
Power transmission in the near field
The concept of waveguide and waveguide modes
Rectangular metallic waveguides and optical fibers
Use of an electromagnetic simulator to study transmission lines, free-space propagation, and antennas
Use of network analyzers to measure characteristic parameters of transmission lines and antennas
teaching_methods: Exercises solved by the instructor in class
Laboratory activities in groups of 2–3 students
assessment_rules: Assessment is based on a written exam lasting approximately 75 minutes, consisting of either two exercises and one open-ended theoretical question or three exercises covering the three main topics. The final grade is determined by the written exam score, increased by a variable percentage based on homework (0% to 5%), self-assessments (0% to 10%), and lab reports (0% to 5%). A total score (written exam plus bonuses) equal to or greater than 33/30 will result in honors being awarded.
